title: Establish provider adapters and server-side session lifecycle

purpose: Provide the narrow server-side provider and session primitives required by the real login and invitation HTTP path.
success_outcome: Both accepted providers cross one normalized, server-only adapter boundary; Identity & Access resolves verified identities, accepts invitations, issues/revokes sessions, and leaves no partial state on failure.
anti_goals: Do not add browser routes, UI authorization, or a dev-login bypass.
Do not expose provider secrets or write Identity & Access state from an adapter.
Do not change the accepted modular-monolith, one-server, or shared-database architecture.

stop_conditions: Stop and route to /spec-design if provider support requires a new service, store, event bus, or change to the accepted module ownership graph.
Stop if a provider response cannot be verified server-side without trusting caller-supplied account, role, center, membership, or invitation data.

constraints: Provider adapters are server-only and return only normalized verified identity.
Identity & Access exclusively writes external identities, invitations, and sessions.
Tests use isolated disposable state and injected provider doubles; no credentials or production database are required for the claim proof.
invariants: One provider identity maps to at most one internal account.
A session is issued only after verified identity resolution or atomic invitation binding.
Invalid provider operations and failed session/binding transactions leave state unchanged.
